findings.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:157 — [confidence 100][P2] `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty());` runs without joining the reader started by `}).start();`, so an in-flight group read that fails after `deletedAll.set(true);` records its exception after the assertion and the regression test passes despite the HTTP failure it claims to detect.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:153 — [confidence 100][P2][advisory] When `managedRealm.admin().groups().group(groupUuid).remove();` throws, execution skips `deletedAll.set(true);` and leaves the untracked non-daemon reader in `while (!deletedAll.get())` issuing requests and retaining exceptions beyond test teardown, burdening subsequent tests and preventing normal JVM shutdown; the strongest rebuttal is that deletion succeeds on the happy path, but failure during a concurrency regression is precisely when cleanup must stop and join the reader in a finally block.

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real defect in the test code. Looking at the diff, the test creates a reader thread with `while (!deletedAll.get())` that runs until `deletedAll.set(true)` is called. However, `deletedAll.set(true)` is only called after the forEach loop that deletes groups. If any `remove()` call throws an exception, the `deletedAll.set(true)` line is never reached, leaving the reader thread running indefinitely. The thread is not a daemon thread and there's no finally block or try-catch to ensure cleanup. This is a real bug in the test code that could cause test pollution and prevent JVM shutdown.
